assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new classification of quantum matter based on band topology and spin-orbit coupling. The Kane-Mele quantum spin Hall proposal, the HgTe/CdTe realisation and the later three-dimensional materials form one of the most influential developments in condensed matter. The concepts are clear, original and have spread into superconducting, photonic and quantum-information platforms.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the decisive theoretical insight. Molenkamp's group gave the first transport observation of the edge channels in HgTe wells (guided by the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, which is not in the credited names). Hasan's work on the three-dimensional materials is also strong and could displace Mele; the configuration is therefore not unique and I choose the two-theorist plus one-experiment version.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than fifteen years of independent confirmation across materials and measurements, and a stable interpretation. Recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: The credit among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp and Hasan, and the omission of Bernevig, Zhang and others from the supplied names, is genuinely contested.
I am relying on recollection of the chronology of the 2D versus 3D discoveries and have not verified it independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal made trapped-ion quantum gates concrete, and ion traps remain one of the leading quantum-computing and simulation platforms with the highest gate fidelities. The work links theory of quantum information to precision experimental control and has had lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the clear originators of the gate proposal. Blatt's group is among the leading experimental groups that realised gates, entanglement and digital simulation with ions. Wineland and Haroche were already recognised in 2012 for ion and cavity control, which narrows what is left to award; Wineland and others (e.g. Monroe) are not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with large independent experimental confirmation and a wide body of follow-on work, though the field is still advancing toward error-corrected devices.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with Zoller's appearance on other candidates (B017, B031) raises a question of how many prizes can be built around him.
Whether the quantum-computing impact is already a demonstrated technology rather than a promise is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong light-matter coupling possible on a chip and is the architecture behind most superconducting quantum processors. The theory proposal and first experimental demonstration of strong coupling, followed by transmon-based readout and control, are of great importance for quantum technology and for microwave quantum optics.
assessment.attribution: Blais supplied the theory proposal, Wallraff and Schoelkopf the first strong-coupling experiments and the later transmon work. Credit is well defined, although the transmon (Koch, Schoelkopf and collaborators) and Yale/ETH contributions are intertwined with the 2025 laureates' circuit work and others who are not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: The field is clearly mature and independently confirmed, but the 2025 prize recognised closely related superconducting-circuit physics, so a prize this soon in the same area may be considered premature by some members.
uncertainties: Closeness to the 2025 prize and to my own research area calls for caution about proximity to this topic.
Whether the committee wishes to recognise a second superconducting-circuit prize so soon is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantised conductance in ballistic point contacts was a clean and fundamental demonstration of Landauer-type conductance quantisation in mesoscopic systems, and it underlies much of electron quantum optics and the design of semiconductor and superconducting nanodevices. The discovery was simple, original and has had a long lasting effect.
assessment.attribution: Two groups, Delft-Philips (van Wees and collaborators) and Cambridge (Wharam, Pepper and collaborators), reported the effect independently and almost simultaneously in 1988. A fair allocation is plausible with names from both groups, but van Wees and Wharam were early-career authors and the role of other co-authors and of theoretical predecessors is unclear.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of confirmation, though the discovery is old enough that its timeliness could be questioned.
uncertainties: Which co-authors in each group made the decisive contribution is not resolved from the supplied names.
The theory background (Landauer, Buttiker) is not represented in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg blockade and tweezer arrays give programmable many-body quantum simulators and emerging quantum processors with hundreds of atoms. The combination of theoretical gate proposals and experimental arrays has opened a new route to quantum computing and quantum simulation.
assessment.attribution: The idea of Rydberg gates (Jaksch, Zoller and collaborators), the blockade demonstrations and the programmable arrays are spread across several groups. Lukin, Browaeys and Zoller cover theory and the main experimental array lines, but Saffman is an equally plausible choice and some of the key proposers are not credited.
assessment.maturity: The platform is developing rapidly and independent replication is growing, but the field is still maturing and error-corrected performance has not yet been shown at scale, so timing may be early.
uncertainties: Attribution is spread over many contributors and the supplied names omit some originators.
The lasting impact of programmable arrays relative to other platforms is not yet clear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene created a tunable platform for correlated insulators and superconductivity, and spawned the whole field of moiré materials. The prediction of flat bands and the experimental observation are both striking.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle, and Jarillo-Herrero's group observed correlated insulators and superconductivity. Andrei's earlier experimental work on twisted graphene is a competing claim to a seat, so allocation is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally reproduced by many groups, but the interpretation of the superconducting mechanism is still unsettled, which makes it somewhat early.
uncertainties: The mechanism of the superconductivity and the competing role of other experiments, for example by Andrei, are open.
Recognition may be premature relative to older candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution is a conceptually important application of quantum mechanics to information security, built around BB84 and entanglement-based protocols, with many experimental implementations and growing commercial and satellite links.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard introduced BB84 and Ekert the entanglement-based protocol, giving a natural three-person configuration. Pan's experimental satellite and long-distance work is strong, but a fourth name would exceed the prize limit.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are mature and widely confirmed, but the practical security of real devices and the scale of technological impact remain debated, and the prize may fit other categories better.
uncertainties: The size of the practical impact relative to its conceptual importance is unclear.
Priority between Ekert's and other authors' entanglement-based protocols could be debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Loss-DiVincenzo and Kane proposals started the field of semiconductor spin qubits, which now have high-fidelity gates in silicon and germanium and are a serious route to scalable quantum processors.
assessment.attribution: Loss and DiVincenzo proposed quantum-dot spin qubits and Kane the donor-based silicon scheme. The proposals are distinct but linked, and many experimental groups made the realisations possible, so an experimental laureate may be needed.
assessment.maturity: Proposals date from 1998 and the experimental platform is progressing quickly but has not yet reached maturity comparable to superconducting or ion platforms.
uncertainties: Impact is still prospective and strongly dependent on the future of silicon quantum computing.
Experimental credit is not represented in the supplied names.
